# core/json.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/json.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

JSON (RFC 8259) read from bytes that cannot be trusted.
Nothing is allocated to check a document: `json_value` returns where the
value that starts at an offset ends, and the readers return offsets into
the same buffer. Objects and arrays nest at most 32 deep. `JsonOut` (the
`json_out_*` calls) writes a document the other way: it tracks commas, keys
and nesting, so what `json_out_finish` returns is well-formed or `None`.

What is proved: no read is outside the buffer, no arithmetic overflows, and
every offset returned lies inside the buffer and after the one it came
from. Not proved: that exactly the documents of RFC 8259 are accepted. The
scanner is strict (no comments, no trailing commas, no leading zeros, no
control characters in strings, no single quotes), but it does not check
that the bytes of a string are UTF-8 and it accepts an escaped surrogate on
its own (`json_string` refuses it). A key with an escape in it is compared
by the bytes as written.

`import "core/json.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/num.bastio](core-num.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`json_ws`](#json_ws) | The first offset at or after `at` that is not JSON whitespace (space, tab, line feed, carriage return). |
| [`json_value`](#json_value) | Where the value that starts at the first non-blank byte at or after `at` ends, past the blanks that follow it. |
| [`json_member`](#json_member) | The offset of the value of the member `key` of the object that starts at the first non-blank byte at or after `at`, or `None` when there is no such member or the document is damaged. |
| [`json_element`](#json_element) | The offset of element number `idx` (from 0) of the array that starts at the first non-blank byte at or after `at`, or `None` when there are fewer elements or the document is damaged. |
| [`json_u64`](#json_u64) | The value at the first non-blank byte at or after `at`, read as a JSON number made only of digits (no sign, fraction or exponent) that fits in a `u64`. |
| [`json_string`](#json_string) | The string at the first non-blank byte at or after `at`, with its escapes decoded (`\u` escapes become UTF-8; a surrogate pair becomes one code point). |
| [`json_push_string`](#json_push_string) | Appends `b` to `t` as a JSON string. |
| [`json_out_new`](#json_out_new) | A new, empty writer. |

## Types and constants

### `Json`

```bastio
enum Json {
  // The value ends here (the offset after its last byte).
  Ok(u64),
  // The input ends inside the value.
  Partial,
  // The value is invalid at this offset.
  Bad(u64),
}
```

What `json_value` found.

### `JsonOut`

```bastio
struct JsonOut {
  text: Vec[u8],
  // Bit `d` is 1 when the container at depth `d` is an object.
  obj: u64,
  // Bit `d` is 1 when the container at depth `d` already has an element.
  full: u64,
  // How many containers are open (at most 32).
  depth: u64,
  // A key was written and its value has not been.
  key: bool,
  // The top-level value is complete.
  done: bool,
  // Some call did not fit.
  bad: bool,
}
```

A JSON document being written. Build it with the `json_out_*` calls and
take it with `json_out_finish`; the writer keeps track of where commas go
and which values may come next, so what comes out is a well-formed
document or nothing. A call that does not fit the place it is made (a
value in an object without a key before it, a key in an array, an end with
nothing open, nesting deeper than 32, a second top-level value) writes
nothing and makes `json_out_finish` return `None`.

## Functions

### `json_ws`

```bastio
fn json_ws(s: &Bytes, at: u64) -> u64
  requires at <= blen(s)
  ensures at <= result && result <= blen(s)
```

The first offset at or after `at` that is not JSON whitespace (space, tab,
line feed, carriage return).

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom(" \t\r\n[1]");
let i = json_ws(b, 0);
let j = json_ws(b, i);
bfree(b);
if i != 4 || j != 4 { return 1; }
```

### `json_value`

```bastio
fn json_value(s: &Bytes, at: u64) -> Json
  requires at <= blen(s)
  ensures result is Json::Ok ==> at < result.Ok && result.Ok <= blen(s)
  ensures result is Json::Bad ==> result.Bad <= blen(s)
```

Where the value that starts at the first non-blank byte at or after `at`
ends, past the blanks that follow it. The whole value is checked, nested objects and arrays included.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom(" {\"a\": [1, 2.5e3, true, null], \"b\": \"x\\n\"} tail");
let mut e = 0;
match json_value(b, 0) {
  Json::Ok(x) => { e = x; },
  Json::Partial => {},
  Json::Bad(x) => {},
}
let cut = bfrom("[1, 2");
let bad = bfrom("[1,]");
let mut p = false;
match json_value(cut, 0) { Json::Partial => { p = true; }, Json::Ok(x) => {}, Json::Bad(x) => {} }
let mut q = 99;
match json_value(bad, 0) { Json::Bad(x) => { q = x; }, Json::Ok(x) => {}, Json::Partial => {} }
bfree(b);
bfree(cut);
bfree(bad);
if e != 43 || !p || q != 3 { return 1; }
```

### `json_member`

```bastio
fn json_member(s: &Bytes, at: u64, key: Str) -> Option[u64]
  requires at <= blen(s)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> at < result.Some && result.Some < blen(s)
```

The offset of the value of the member `key` of the object that starts at
the first non-blank byte at or after `at`, or `None` when there is no such
member or the document is damaged. The first member of that name wins. Keys
are compared by the bytes as written, so a key written with an escape
does not match its unescaped spelling.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("{\"a\": 1, \"b\": {\"a\": 2}, \"c\": [true]}");
let mut c = 0;
match json_member(b, 0, "c") { Option::Some(x) => { c = x; }, Option::None => {} }
let gone = json_member(b, 0, "d");
let onearr = json_member(b, c, "a");   // `c` is an array, not an object
bfree(b);
if c != 29 || gone is Option::Some || onearr is Option::Some { return 1; }
```

### `json_element`

```bastio
fn json_element(s: &Bytes, at: u64, idx: u64) -> Option[u64]
  requires at <= blen(s)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> at < result.Some && result.Some < blen(s)
```

The offset of element number `idx` (from 0) of the array that starts at the
first non-blank byte at or after `at`, or `None` when there are fewer
elements or the document is damaged.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("[10, [1, 2], \"x\", null]");
let mut third = 0;
match json_element(b, 0, 2) { Option::Some(x) => { third = x; }, Option::None => {} }
let past = json_element(b, 0, 4);
bfree(b);
if third != 13 || past is Option::Some { return 1; }
```

### `json_u64`

```bastio
fn json_u64(s: &Bytes, at: u64) -> Option[u64]
  requires at <= blen(s)
```

The value at the first non-blank byte at or after `at`, read as a JSON
number made only of digits (no sign, fraction or exponent) that fits in a
`u64`.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("[42, -1, 1.5, 18446744073709551616]");
let mut a = 0;
match json_u64(b, 1) { Option::Some(x) => { a = x; }, Option::None => {} }
let neg = json_u64(b, 5);
let frac = json_u64(b, 9);
let big = json_u64(b, 14);
bfree(b);
if a != 42 || neg is Option::Some || frac is Option::Some || big is Option::Some { return 1; }
```

### `json_string`

```bastio
fn json_string(s: &Bytes, at: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires at <= blen(s)
```

The string at the first non-blank byte at or after `at`, with its escapes
decoded (`\u` escapes become UTF-8; a surrogate pair becomes one code
point). `None` when it is not a string, is cut short, has a bad escape or
holds a surrogate without its partner. The bytes between the escapes are
copied as they are.

Example:

```bastio
let b = bfrom("\"a\\n\\u00e9\\ud83d\\ude00\"");
let mut ok = false;
match json_string(b, 0) {
  Option::Some(v) => { ok = blen(v) == 8 && bget(v, 1) == 10 && bget(v, 2) == 195 && bget(v, 3) == 169 && bget(v, 4) == 240 && bget(v, 7) == 128; bfree(v); },
  Option::None => {},
}
let lone = bfrom("\"\\ud800\"");
let mut refused = true;
match json_string(lone, 0) {
  Option::Some(v) => { refused = false; bfree(v); },
  Option::None => {},
}
bfree(b);
bfree(lone);
if !ok || !refused { return 1; }
```

### `json_push_string`

```bastio
fn json_push_string(t: &mut Vec[u8], b: &Bytes)
```

Appends `b` to `t` as a JSON string: in quotes, with `"` and `\` escaped,
and the control characters below 32 as `\n`, `\r`, `\t` or `\u00XX`. Other
bytes, UTF-8 included, are copied as they are.

Example:

```bastio
let mut v = bfrom("a\"b\\\n.");
bset(&mut v, 5, 1);
let mut t = text_new();
json_push_string(&mut t, v);
let out = text_finish(t);
let ok = bytes_eq_str(out, "\"a\\\"b\\\\\\n\\u0001\"");
bfree(v);
bfree(out);
if !ok { return 1; }
```

### `json_out_new`

```bastio
fn json_out_new() -> JsonOut
```

A new, empty writer.

Example:

```bastio
let mut o = json_out_new();
json_out_begin_obj(&mut o);
let k = bfrom("n");
json_out_key(&mut o, k);
json_out_u64(&mut o, 7);
json_out_end(&mut o);
bfree(k);
match json_out_finish(o) {
  Option::Some(b) => {
    let ok = bytes_eq_str(b, "{\"n\":7}");
    bfree(b);
    if !ok { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `json_out_begin_obj`

```bastio
fn json_out_begin_obj(o: &mut JsonOut)
```

Opens an object (`{`).

Example:

```bastio
let mut o = json_out_new();
json_out_begin_arr(&mut o);
json_out_begin_obj(&mut o);
json_out_end(&mut o);
json_out_begin_obj(&mut o);
json_out_end(&mut o);
json_out_end(&mut o);
match json_out_finish(o) {
  Option::Some(b) => {
    let ok = bytes_eq_str(b, "[{},{}]");
    bfree(b);
    if !ok { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `json_out_begin_arr`

```bastio
fn json_out_begin_arr(o: &mut JsonOut)
```

Opens an array (`[`).

Example:

```bastio
let mut o = json_out_new();
json_out_begin_arr(&mut o);
json_out_u64(&mut o, 1);
json_out_begin_arr(&mut o);
json_out_end(&mut o);
json_out_end(&mut o);
match json_out_finish(o) {
  Option::Some(b) => {
    let ok = bytes_eq_str(b, "[1,[]]");
    bfree(b);
    if !ok { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `json_out_end`

```bastio
fn json_out_end(o: &mut JsonOut)
```

Closes the innermost object or array. With nothing open, or after a key
that has no value yet, the writer goes bad.

Example:

```bastio
let mut o = json_out_new();
json_out_begin_arr(&mut o);
json_out_end(&mut o);
json_out_end(&mut o);   // nothing is open
match json_out_finish(o) {
  Option::Some(b) => { bfree(b); return 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
```

### `json_out_key`

```bastio
fn json_out_key(o: &mut JsonOut, k: &Bytes)
```

Writes the key of the next member of the open object.

Example:

```bastio
let mut o = json_out_new();
json_out_begin_obj(&mut o);
let a = bfrom("a\"b");
let c = bfrom("c");
json_out_key(&mut o, a);
json_out_bool(&mut o, true);
json_out_key(&mut o, c);
json_out_null(&mut o);
json_out_end(&mut o);
bfree(a);
bfree(c);
match json_out_finish(o) {
  Option::Some(b) => {
    let ok = bytes_eq_str(b, "{\"a\\\"b\":true,\"c\":null}");
    bfree(b);
    if !ok { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `json_out_str`

```bastio
fn json_out_str(o: &mut JsonOut, b: &Bytes)
```

Writes a string value, escaped as `json_push_string` does.

Example:

```bastio
let mut o = json_out_new();
let s = bfrom("line\nbreak");
json_out_str(&mut o, s);
bfree(s);
match json_out_finish(o) {
  Option::Some(b) => {
    let ok = bytes_eq_str(b, "\"line\\nbreak\"");
    bfree(b);
    if !ok { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `json_out_bool`

```bastio
fn json_out_bool(o: &mut JsonOut, v: bool)
```

Writes `true` or `false`.

Example:

```bastio
let mut o = json_out_new();
json_out_begin_arr(&mut o);
json_out_bool(&mut o, true);
json_out_bool(&mut o, false);
json_out_end(&mut o);
match json_out_finish(o) {
  Option::Some(b) => {
    let ok = bytes_eq_str(b, "[true,false]");
    bfree(b);
    if !ok { return 1; }
  },
  Option::None => { return 1; },
}
```

### `json_out_null`

```bastio
fn json_out_null(o: &mut JsonOut)
```

Writes `null`.

Example:

```bastio
let mut o = json_out_new();
json_out_null(&mut o);
json_out_null(&mut o);   // a second top-level value does not fit
match json_out_finish(o) {
  Option::Some(b) => { bfree(b); return 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
```

### `json_out_finish`

```bastio
fn json_out_finish(o: JsonOut) -> Option[Bytes]
```

The finished document, or `None` when a call did not fit or the document
is not complete (a container still open, nothing written).

Example:

```bastio
let mut o = json_out_new();
json_out_begin_arr(&mut o);   // never closed
match json_out_finish(o) {
  Option::Some(b) => { bfree(b); return 1; },
  Option::None => {},
}
```

## Internals

### `json_str_end`

```bastio
fn json_str_end(s: &Bytes, p: u64) -> Json
  requires p < blen(s)
  ensures result is Json::Ok ==> p + 2 <= result.Ok && result.Ok <= blen(s)
  ensures result is Json::Bad ==> result.Bad <= blen(s)
```

Internal: the end of the string whose opening quote is at `p`.

### `json_num_end`

```bastio
fn json_num_end(s: &Bytes, p: u64) -> Json
  requires p < blen(s)
  ensures result is Json::Ok ==> p < result.Ok && result.Ok <= blen(s)
  ensures result is Json::Bad ==> result.Bad <= blen(s)
```

Internal: the end of the number that starts at `p`.

### `json_lit_end`

```bastio
fn json_lit_end(s: &Bytes, p: u64, lit: Str) -> Json
  requires p < blen(s)
  ensures result is Json::Ok ==> p < result.Ok && result.Ok <= blen(s)
  ensures result is Json::Bad ==> result.Bad <= blen(s)
```

Internal: the end of the literal `lit` (`true`, `false`, `null`) at `p`.

### `json_hex4`

```bastio
fn json_hex4(s: &Bytes, i: u64) -> Option[u64]
  requires i + 4 <= blen(s)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> result.Some <= 65535
```

Internal: the four hexadecimal digits at `i`, or `None`.

### `json_put_utf8`

```bastio
fn json_put_utf8(t: &mut Vec[u8], cp: u64)
  requires cp <= 1114111
```

Internal: appends the UTF-8 encoding of the code point `cp`.

### `json_out_slot`

```bastio
fn json_out_slot(o: &mut JsonOut) -> bool
```

Internal: makes room for a value at the current place: writes the comma
an array element needs, and returns false (and marks the writer bad) when
no value may come here. At the top level the value counts as done; a
container resets that until it is closed.

### `json_out_open`

```bastio
fn json_out_open(o: &mut JsonOut, open: u8, is_obj: bool)
```

Internal: opens a container (`open` is `{` or `[`, `is_obj` says which).
